ADR-0015 (schema scope: monolithic) and ADR-0016 (Verifier interface) accepted; both blocked_on_decision references cleared by commit d5a9e63. Five human-checkpoint tasks (p2-t01, p2-t05, p2-t07, p2-t10, p2-t11, p2-t13) require approvals.json entries. Read APPROVAL.md before re-editing.

tasks.title: Implement Drizzle schema for all ten tech-spec §4 tables (node, edge, obligation, lease+fence_seq, task_active view, event_log, trace_event, retrieval, row_audit, vec0 virtuals) per the scope decided in ADR-0015 — schema only, no migrations yet
tasks.notes: **Architectural surface — flagged human_checkpoint.** Schema decisions cascade through Phases 3-5. ADR-0015 (Accepted 2026-04-27) decided monolithic — ten tables now, empty for the phase-4/5 ones. The agent drafts the schema following ADR-0015; the human reviews column types, FK semantics, CHECK constraints, and STRICT/WITHOUT ROWID conventions against tech-spec §4 before approving. After approval, p2-t02 runs `drizzle-kit generate` for the first migration.

tasks.title: Generate first Drizzle migration from the approved schema and confirm `atlas migrate lint --latest 1` exits 0
Implement WAL pragmas + sqlite-vec attach in db/init.ts; backup-before-migrate refuses to start if backup write fails
tasks.notes: Pragmas: journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, mmap_size=268435456, temp_store=MEMORY, foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=5000. Tests: pragma values readable post-init; sqlite-vec virtual table createable; backup write failure causes refuse-to-start.

tasks.title: Implement /spec/*.md frontmatter parser → graph nodes (intents, constraints, decisions, concepts)
tasks.notes: Use the YAML frontmatter schemas already documented in /spec/*/README.md and ADR-0009. Parse all four kinds present under /spec/: intent, constraint, decision, AND concept (the Daniel Jackson concept boundaries from tech-spec §3.5 line 141 and §4.1's 'concept' node kind — the original draft missed this). Add 1-2 example intents and 1 example concept under spec/ so the parser has fixtures and the team can see the dogfood loop. The 'realizes' edge connecting intents to concepts is parsed from frontmatter `parent` per ADR-0009. Real intents (the L0 dogfood payload) are authored in p2-t11.

tasks.title: Implement tree-sitter native walk of packages/*/src/** producing code-symbol nodes with stable IDs
tasks.notes: **Symbol identity is load-bearing — flagged human_checkpoint.** Use SCIP-first when available; composite-heuristic fallback (sig 0.30 + body 0.35 + outgoing-call 0.20 + name 0.15) with thresholds 0.85/0.65 per tech-spec §3.2. Human reviews the heuristic implementation before approving.

tasks.title: Implement build-graph.ts that emits graph.json + seeds the SQLite DB from /spec parser + tree-sitter walk
Implement Coverage Verifier: every Intent has ≥1 `realizes` edge and every Constraint has a `verified_by` link — first concrete verifier against the Verifier interface
tasks.notes:
**Architectural surface — flagged human_checkpoint.** This task lands the Coverage Verifier AND the Verifier interface contract that all later verifiers inherit. ADR-0016 (Accepted 2026-04-27) decided: interface in @intentgraph/shared/verifier/ so MCP plugins can import it without dragging skill internals; builtins under packages/skill/src/verifiers/builtin/; scheduler.ts free function for sub-ms/ms + Inngest wrap for s/minutes; registry.ts is the module-load barrel for builtins; third-party plugins go through the verify.run MCP tool, no separate verifier.register. The scope_files in this task reflect that decision.

**L0-completion semantics — bootstrap problem resolved as: Coverage Verifier failures SURFACE AS WARNINGS in phase 2, NOT BLOCKERS for L0.** Reasoning: the L0 gate (tech-spec line 445) is 'IntentGraph's own intents and code modules are visible' + '60s findability', not 'every intent has a realizes edge'. A green Coverage run on an empty / partially-authored intent set is meaningless; a red Coverage run on the in-progress dogfood payload (p2-t11) is expected and useful as triage. Phase 3 (L1) raises Coverage to a CI gate once bidirectional sync makes intent-edge authoring cheap. Implementation: Coverage Verifier writes findings to obligation table with status='failed' (not 'rejected') and the L0 checklist (p2-t10) reads them as informational. The CI escalation lands in phase-3 task list, not here.

tasks.title: Wire the webview to read graph.json (still file-based for L0); add Contextual Zoom LOD and ELK-in-worker integration
tasks.notes: L0 reads the file directly; the MCP path is Phase 3. Implement Contextual Zoom LOD (3 tiers tied to useViewport()) and onlyRenderVisibleElements per tech-spec §3.3.

tasks.title: Sub-flows for concept boundaries (extent: 'parent') with example concept node grouping intents/constraints
L0 acceptance: produce CHECKLIST showing IntentGraph's own intents and code modules visible in `pnpm build && open app/dist/index.html`; new team member finds an intent in <60s
tasks.notes: L0 gate is the dogfooding gate (tech-spec line 445). Agent produces the checklist; human runs it and signs off. Without this signoff, Phase 3 cannot start. The checklist's 'find an intent in 60s' criterion only makes sense once p2-t11 has authored real intents under /spec/intents/ (the L0 dogfood payload), which is why p2-t10 depends on p2-t11. Coverage Verifier output (p2-t07) appears as informational warnings per the bootstrap-resolution note in p2-t07; the checklist surfaces those without treating them as gate failures.

tasks.title: Author IntentGraph's own intents under /spec/intents/ — the L0 dogfood payload (~10 intents covering the five pillars)
tasks.notes: **The L0 gate is meaningless without real intents.** tech-spec line 445 says the L0 acceptance is 'IntentGraph's own intents and code modules are visible' and 'a new team member finds an intent visually within 60s' — both presuppose the team's actual intents exist as authored markdown. Author ~10 intents covering the five architectural pillars (CLAUDE.md), with realizes-edges to /spec/concepts/ entries and verified_by links from /spec/constraints/ entries. Use the frontmatter schema from ADR-0009 and the parser fixtures from p2-t04 as templates. **Human_checkpoint** because this is product authorship — the agent can draft, but the human must edit for accuracy + own the content. The architect skill should review whether each intent is outcome-focused (per intentgraph-spec-writer's discipline). p2-t10 cannot start until this lands.

tasks.title: Risk-C spike step 1: synthesize 5k-node graph generator script + run through ELK worker harness
tasks.notes: First half of the Risk-C spike (tech-spec §7-C). Synthesize a 5k-node graph (use ULIDs + the 9 node kinds + realistic edge density, ~3 edges/node) and a runner that invokes the ELK worker from p2-t08 against it. Output is the script + harness only — no measurements yet. Splitting the spike into generator (this task) + measurement+recommendation (p2-t12b) keeps each task within the schema's 60-min cap and lets the human review the synthetic graph's realism before measurement results bias the discussion.

tasks.title: Risk-C spike step 2: measure ELK timing on the 5k-node harness + write findings + recommend incremental-vs-server-side strategy
tasks.notes: Second half of the Risk-C spike. Run the p2-t12a harness, record p50/p95/p99 layout time on a typical dev machine. Write findings to docs/spikes/elk-5k-results.md with a recommendation: keep the incremental local placement strategy (§3.5 line 142), OR escalate to server-side ELK for >3k-node graphs (§6 phase 6 already foreshadows this), OR add the Sigma.js overview escape hatch sooner. **Human_checkpoint** because if the recommendation is 'change the strategy,' an ADR must open before phase 3 — that decision is too load-bearing for the loop to commit autonomously. If the recommendation is 'keep the existing strategy,' the human can sign off and the loop proceeds.

tasks.title: Tree-sitter grammar pinning + ERROR/MISSING-node handling per tech-spec §7-J
tasks.notes: tech-spec §7-J: 'A TS 5.x feature may not parse on an older grammar. Pin grammar versions and treat ERROR/MISSING nodes as first-class "unknown skeleton" nodes rather than failing.' Pin tree-sitter and tree-sitter-typescript to exact versions in packages/skill/package.json (no caret), document the pinned versions in grammar-registry.ts with a one-line provenance comment, and implement an error-nodes.ts module that converts ERROR / MISSING tree-sitter nodes into 'unknown_skeleton' code-symbol nodes (kind='code_symbol', confidence='extracted', body includes the raw range so future drift detection can reason about the skeleton). Tests: a TS file with intentional syntax errors parses to an unknown_skeleton node rather than throwing.
